title: Exodus — Civilian Evacuation Risk Platform
summary: A single FastAPI web platform for civilian-evacuation planning that unifies a crisis map, the ERCF scenario cost model and the CERAI risk assessment behind one backend and interface.

contribution.roleNote: Unifies Ethical Tech CoLab tools: EII, ERCF, CERAI and the route and behavioral simulators.

narrative.problem: Civilian-evacuation risk tools built separately, a crisis-information map, a scenario cost model and a risk anticipation index, each answer part of the question and run on their own backends, data sources and keys, so a planner has to move between them.
narrative.decision: Brings the three tools together as tabs of one FastAPI application, so all three share one backend, one design language and one set of API keys, with scenario storage in SQLite.
narrative.tradeoff: The platform carries copies of its component models that must be re-synced when their upstream repositories change, and its live features depend on several third-party services (INFORM/ACAPS, ACLED, Tavily, GDELT, Anthropic), with fallbacks when keys are missing.
narrative.limitation: The README documents no evaluation, tests or limitations of its own, and the CoLab's After the Corridor report lists Exodus as built and operational but not yet validated.
narrative.caveat: Country analysis is AI-generated (Claude, with a fallback), and live news and conflict data depend on third-party API keys; the platform is not validated for operational evacuation decisions.
